decks.module: Work zone conduct and regulatory signs
decks.domain: Rules of the road: work zone conduct, regulatory, guide and route signs, pavement markings, lane controls, crosswalks and stop lines

cards.front: What does the manual mean by giving construction workers a brake?
cards.back: The manual asks drivers to give construction workers a brake: slow down in work zones and be ready to stop suddenly.

cards.front: What following habit does the manual forbid in work zones?
cards.back: Do not tailgate other vehicles in a work zone.

cards.front: What can happen to a driver who endangers a highway worker?
cards.back: A driver who endangers a highway worker may be fined and have points added to their driving record, under SC Code §fifty-six-five-one thousand five hundred thirty-five.

cards.front: What shapes and colors are regulatory signs?
cards.back: Regulatory signs are square, rectangular or a special shape, and they are white with black, red or green letters or symbols.

cards.front: What do regulatory signs tell you?
cards.back: Regulatory signs state specific laws you must obey, covering matters such as traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed and parking.

cards.front: What does a red circle with a red slash on a regulatory sign mean?
cards.back: A regulatory sign showing a red circle with a red slash across a symbol prohibits the action pictured.

cards.front: How does a plain regulatory sign differ from one with a red circle and slash?
cards.back: Regulatory signs in general state laws you must follow, while the version with a red circle and slash specifically forbids whatever action is pictured beneath it.

cards.front: Which regulatory signs does the manual picture?
cards.back: Common regulatory signs pictured include No U-Turn, No Left Turn, No Right Turn, Left Turn Only, Straight, and Straight or Turn Right.

cards.front: What colors are speed limit signs, and what speed do they give?
cards.back: Speed limit signs are black and white and give the maximum legal speed allowed in ideal conditions.

cards.front: What do black-and-white speed limit signs indicate?
cards.back: Speed limit signs are black-and-white signs showing the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions.

decks.domain: Rules of the road: work zone conduct, regulatory, guide and route signs, pavement markings, lane controls, crosswalks and stop lines

cards.front: What shape and colors identify a stop sign?
cards.back: A stop sign is red with white letters and has eight sides.

cards.front: Where do you stop at a stop sign?
cards.back: At a stop sign you stop behind the stop line, or behind the crosswalk if there is one.

cards.front: Where do you stop at a stop sign with no stop line?
cards.back: Where a stop sign has no stop line, stop at the point closest to the intersection from which you can see both ways without pulling into the cross traffic lane.

cards.front: What must you do after stopping at a stop sign?
cards.back: After stopping at a stop sign, look in all directions for crossing vehicles and pedestrians and yield the right-of-way.

cards.front: How can you tell a stop sign from a yield sign by shape?
cards.back: The stop sign is a red octagon with white letters, while the yield sign is a downward-pointing red and white triangle whose letters are red.

cards.front: What does a yield sign look like and require?
cards.back: A yield sign is a red and white triangle pointing downward with red letters, and it means slow down and let traffic that has the right-of-way cross before you enter.
cards.memory_hook: Slow down and let them pass

cards.front: How do the duties at a stop sign and a yield sign differ?
cards.back: A stop sign requires a stop and then yielding, whereas a yield sign requires slowing and letting right-of-way traffic cross before you enter.

cards.front: Who may use a lane marked by the Shared Center Lane Left Turn Only sign?
cards.back: The Shared Center Lane Left Turn Only sign marks a lane reserved for vehicles turning left from either direction, and it is not for through traffic or for passing.

cards.front: What do one-way street signs tell you?
cards.back: One-way street signs show that traffic moves only in the arrow's direction, so never turn against the arrow or drive the wrong way on a one-way street.

decks.domain: Rules of the road: work zone conduct, regulatory, guide and route signs, pavement markings, lane controls, crosswalks and stop lines

cards.front: What shapes and colors are guide signs?
cards.back: Guide signs are square or rectangular and colored green, brown or blue.

cards.front: What shapes, colors, and purposes identify guide signs?
cards.back: Guide signs are square or rectangular signs in green, brown, or blue that give intersecting-road information, directions to cities and towns, points of interest, and locations of hospitals, service stations, restaurants, and hotels.

cards.front: What information do guide signs give?
cards.back: Guide signs give information on intersecting roads, point you toward cities and towns, show points of interest and help you find hospitals, service stations, restaurants and hotels.

cards.front: What do the shape and color of a route number sign show?
cards.back: The shape and color of a route number sign show the type of road it marks: interstate, US, state, city, county or local.

cards.front: How should you plan and follow a trip route?
cards.back: Plan a trip with a road map or GPS device, then follow the route signs during the trip so you do not get lost in an unfamiliar area.

cards.front: Which route number signs does the manual picture?
cards.back: Route number signs pictured include Interstate Route, US Route and State Route signs, along with the Secondary System Road Marker.

cards.front: How do you read the numbers on a Secondary System Road Marker?
cards.back: On a Secondary System Road Marker, the number right after the letter S tells you which county the road lies in, and the final number identifies the road itself.

cards.front: Which number on the S road marker is the county and which is the road?
cards.back: On the S road marker the county number comes first and the road number comes last, and each county keeps its own separate set of secondary road numbers.

cards.front: How are secondary road numbers organized across counties?
cards.back: Every county has its own separate set of secondary road numbers.

cards.front: Where can you find every secondary road on a map?
cards.back: All secondary roads appear on county maps, which can be bought by mail from the central office of the Department of Transportation, although the state primary system map shows only a few.

cards.front: What are secondary system roads, and who should avoid them as through routes?
cards.back: Secondary system roads are local roads serving rural and urban traffic, and in rural areas they are not meant as through routes for drivers unfamiliar with the area.

cards.front: Why should drivers unfamiliar with an area avoid rural secondary roads as through routes?
cards.back: In rural areas secondary system roads are not designed as through routes, which is why drivers who do not know the area should not normally use them.

cards.front: What does the Evacuation Route sign mark?
cards.back: If a hurricane strikes, a mandatory evacuation may be declared for South Carolina's coastal areas, and the Evacuation Route sign marks roads used for that kind of emergency.

decks.domain: Rules of the road: work zone conduct, regulatory, guide and route signs, pavement markings, lane controls, crosswalks and stop lines

cards.front: What are pavement markings?
cards.back: Pavement markings are lines, arrows, words or symbols painted on the road surface to give directions or warnings.

cards.front: What jobs do pavement markings do?
cards.back: Pavement markings divide lanes, show when you may pass or change lanes, show which lanes to use for turns, define pedestrian walkways and show where to stop for signs or signals.

cards.front: What kind of roadway do the yellow lane marking diagrams show?
cards.back: The yellow lane marking diagrams all show two-direction roadways.

cards.front: Which passing situations do the two-direction diagrams show?
cards.back: On two-direction roadways the diagrams show passing prohibited in both directions, passing permitted, and passing permitted only when the dashed line is on your side.

cards.front: On a two-direction road with mixed markings, who may pass?
cards.back: On a two-direction roadway, one yellow marking pattern allows passing only for the driver who has the dashed line on their side.

cards.front: What does the white lane marking diagram show?
cards.back: The white lane marking diagram shows a one-direction roadway on which passing is permitted.

cards.front: Which other lane controls does the manual picture?
cards.back: Other lane controls pictured are the shared center left turn lane and reversible lanes.

decks.domain: Rules of the road: work zone conduct, regulatory, guide and route signs, pavement markings, lane controls, crosswalks and stop lines

cards.front: How many common types of crosswalk markings does the manual picture?
cards.back: The manual pictures three common types of crosswalk markings.

cards.front: What does a crosswalk define?
cards.back: A crosswalk defines the area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

cards.front: Where do you stop when a sign or signal requires it?
cards.back: When a sign or signal makes you stop, stop behind the stop line or crosswalk, and if there is neither, stop at the nearest point where you can see both ways without entering cross traffic.

cards.front: Where is the stopping point when there is no stop line and no crosswalk?
cards.back: With no stop line and no crosswalk, the stopping point is the spot nearest the intersection where you can see both ways without moving into cross traffic.

cards.front: Whom must you yield to at a crosswalk?
cards.back: You must yield to pedestrians who are in a crosswalk or entering one.

cards.front: What should you do where no crosswalk is marked?
cards.back: Not every crosswalk is marked, so watch for pedestrians at intersections, and if no crosswalk is apparent, stop before entering the intersection.

cards.front: When a stop line comes before a crosswalk, which do you obey first?
cards.back: Where a stop line comes before a crosswalk, the stop line must be obeyed first.

cards.front: With both a stop line and a crosswalk, where do you stop?
cards.back: When a stop line and a crosswalk are both present and the stop line comes first, you stop at the stop line rather than at the crosswalk.
cards.memory_hook: At the line, not the crosswalk

recaps.module: Work zone conduct and regulatory signs

recap_hooks.text: Slow down and never tailgate in work zones, and remember that regulatory signs state laws, with a red circle and slash forbidding the pictured action.
A stop sign is a red octagon that means stop and then yield, while a yield sign is a downward triangle that means slow and let traffic pass.
Guide signs are green, brown or blue, and on the S road marker the county number comes first and the road number last.
Yellow markings separate two directions of traffic, white markings sit on one-way roads, and only the dashed side may pass.
Yield to anyone in or entering a crosswalk, and when a stop line comes before the crosswalk, stop at the line.
